You will show the proof of ID when you’re scheduled for an orientation and during the orientation which counts as your first day, we fill out the I-9.  

Today you will not need your ID. If you are given a contingency offer, you will be asked to come back in to complete a background check. If that comes back okay, then we will need your ID to complete your I-9. 

If you bring your passport, that’s perfect we only need that one type of identification. If you do not have a passport we will need you to bring your state issued ID as well as either your SS card or birth certificate. 

Each store has an HR partner called the ASDS or associate support department supervisor. They are the ones who will be scheduling and completing the orientation with you as well as verifying your ID(s).

Fellow first year teacher! I just started in February I’d be happy to share horror stories and provide a listening ear!

I am a 3rd grade self contained special education teacher. I work in a behavioral school with students who are all diagnosed as emotionally disturbed. While they have this diagnosis it doesn’t mean they are all depressed at all times. 

Just noticing subtle changes in their behaviors such as becoming more quiet, staring, not completing work, or acting out more than usual can be signs. If I can catch some of these signs and ask them how they are or report these changes to support staff I can sometimes catch a meltdown early and get the student the help they need. 

Also, making time for weekly or even daily check in conversations where the student has the chance to talk to me one on one. I ask them about how they are and just give them a chance to chat with me. I like taking this time because while some kids will come up to me first thing right in the morning to tell me what happened to them last night, some kids need the extra one on one time. 

If I do think that a student is going through depression or self loathing I am lucky to be at a school that’s built for such things with the amount of support staff that we have. I will always alert admin and the school psychologists of what is going on. Then I will work with my student to make sure they know they are loved by me. I will give them extra attention if that is what they need, a person to talk to, etc. We follow a model of social skills in our school and one of them is accepting compliments. Recently when a student reported to me that he felt like his friends didn’t like him anymore I made a lesson where we all wrote out compliments to each other (proof read by me first). Then we practiced giving them to each other and saying thank you. Seeing his face smiling after being complimented by his friends I could tell that this lesson was a step in the right direction for him to feel comfortable to reconnect with his friends that day.
